newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: YUGOSLAVIA SAYS WHEAT CROP EXCEEDS 3.1 MILLION T.
newsitem.headline: YUGOSLAVIA SAYS WHEAT CROP EXCEEDS 3.1 MILLION T.

text.p: Yugoslavia's 1997 wheat harvest has been completed successfully and the yield is twice as high as the previous year with 3.123 million tonnes gathered from 817,000 hectares, Belgrade daily Borba reported on Monday.

"Average yield is nearly four tonnes per hectare and the rich crop satisfies our food needs and necessary reserves while a surplus of around 300,000 tonnes is earmarked for export," Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic was quoted by the paper as saying.
Average yields would have been higher had bad weather not hampered the harvest.
All the wheat was now stored, Babovic said.
The Serbian government had secured 75 million German marks to buy up the new crop.

Farmers and agricultural firms would be paid in three instalments. The first instalment of 40 percent would be paid immediately while funds had also been secured for payment of the second and third, Babovic said.
